results.label: every JavaScript file the app ships parses and prints twice to the same bytes (94 files)
printing never makes a file longer than it was
the whole corpus gets smaller, and the probe reports by how much
every printed file is accepted by V8 itself (node --check on all 94 outputs)
the syntax corpus parses and re-prints stably (34 constructs)
an unused import becomes a side-effect import (`import "./s.js"`) instead of being deleted, so importing still runs the module
a module keeps its import and export forms through printing and through compression, an exported name is never renamed, and V8 accepts the result as a module
every invalid program is refused with a SyntaxError carrying a line and a column and a message (18 cases)
the position points at the offending token on the right line, 1-based in the message and 0-based in the object
a tree too deep for V8's stack is refused in words (a SyntaxError that says it nests too deeply), never as a raw RangeError
the depth a hand-written file could plausibly reach is handled: 500 nested parentheses, 500 nested blocks and a 500-term chain all compress
large but plausible input completes inside its time budget and is stable on a second pass
a BOM, CRLF, escaped identifiers, astral characters and $/_ names all survive a round trip
the source map counts CRLF input as two lines, not one, so its original lines are right

scope: the parser and the printer on their own: every shipped file, a curated syntax corpus, eighteen invalid programs that must be refused with a position, deep and huge input, and the awkward characters (BOM, CRLF, astral, escaped identifiers). Behavioural equivalence is the differential probe's job, not this one's.
